page.layout: One page of text, set as verse in lines with alternating indents, with page number 349 at the head and catchword "Seris" at the lower right.

main_text.p: Fortuna prauos usq; & usq; inebriat. Tu mentem ab ira contine: Ne forte mens patrare quiduis impotens, Labatur in scelus graue.
Nam iustus orbis arbiter delet malos: At spem locantes in Deum, Longæua terras incolent in secula, Seriscq; tradent posteris.
Breue ecce tempus, nusquam erunt & impij, Nec umbra uanæ gloriæ Quæsita restabit. Sed usq; exerciti Diris pij periculis,
Terras in alto possidebunt otio, Et posteris linquent suis.
Vtcunq; dente infrendat impius truci, Bonisq; construat dolos, Cladem imminentem prouidens eius Deus, Deridet irritas minas.
Intendit arcum, & stringit ensem, gestiens Vt maclet[?] insidijs pium: At ense proprio cadet, tum spicula Frangentur arcus noxij.
Angusta pauperum iuuat plus recula, Quæsita rectis artibus, Quàm diuitum, congesta per nefarium Scelus, superba copia.
Nam conteretur fastus omnis impij, at Suos Deus tuebitur:

page.notes: Lines alternate between flush-left and indented; I have grouped each flush line with the indented line that follows as one verse paragraph, since the page gives no stanza break. "maclet" is doubtful, as are the underlined words (Quæsita, Suos, Seris) which may be marked in the print rather than italic. Long s is plain s throughout. The catchword "Seris" is in heavier type at the lower right.
